procedure: Dry a reaction flask and maintain under nitrogen or argon. Charge the flask with CNC(=O)[C@@H](N)Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12, 1.00 equivalent, and anhydrous dichloromethane, using about 8 mL per mmol of amine.
Add triethylamine, 1.20 equivalents, and cool the mixture to 0 °C.

Add the isocyanate solution dropwise at 0 °C over approximately 0.25 h.
Stir at 0 °C for 0.5 h, then allow the reaction to warm to 20 °C and stir for 16 h.
Monitor reaction completion by LCMS or TLC. If residual isocyanate remains, a small amount of methanol may be added cautiously to quench it after completion of the desired reaction.

Concentrate or dilute with dichloromethane, then wash the organic layer with water or saturated ammonium chloride, followed by brine. Dry over sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate and remove solvent under reduced pressure.

reagents.name: 3-Chlorophenyl isocyanate
reagents.quantity_for_1_mmol_scale: 161 mg, approximately 0.13 mL depending on density

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge an oven-dried flask with CNC(=O)[C@@H](N)Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12.Cl, 1.0 equiv, and dry dichloromethane, 10 mL per mmol. Cool to 0 °C and add triethylamine, 2.2 equiv, dropwise with stirring. After 10 minutes, add 3-chlorophenyl isocyanate, 1.05 equiv, dropwise at 0 °C. Stir for 15 minutes at 0 °C, then allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 3 hours. Monitor by LCMS or TLC until the amine is consumed. Quench cautiously with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride or water, separate the organic layer, and extract the aqueous phase with dichloromethane. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol or ethyl acetate/hexane with a small amount of triethylamine if needed to minimize tailing, giving CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)Nc1cccc(Cl)c1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Urea formation by addition of an alpha-amino amide to 3-chlorophenyl isocyanate

solvents.name: anhydrous dichloromethane
solvents.volume: 10 mL per 1.0 mmol of amine substrate

reaction_conditions.time: 4 hours total: 0.5 hours at 0 °C, then 3.5 hours at 23 °C

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, dry a flask and maintain under nitrogen or argon. Add L-tryptophan N-methylamide free amine, CNC(=O)[C@@H](N)Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12, 1.0 equiv, and anhydrous dichloromethane, using about 8 mL initially. Cool the suspension or solution to 0 °C. Prepare a solution of 3-chlorophenyl isocyanate, O=C=Nc1cccc(Cl)c1, 1.05 equiv, in about 2 mL anhydrous dichloromethane and add it dropwise at 0 °C. Stir for 30 minutes at 0 °C, then allow the mixture to warm to 23 °C and stir for 3.5 hours. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC until the amine is consumed. Quench any residual isocyanate with a small amount of methanol, then concentrate or dilute with dichloromethane and wash with water/brine as appropriate. Dry the organic phase over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol, or by trituration/preparative HPLC if needed, to obtain CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)Nc1cccc(Cl)c1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Urea formation by addition of a free alpha-amino amide to 3-chlorophenyl isocyanate

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Best route: use the free alpha-amino tryptophan N-methylamide scaffold and react it directly with 3-chlorophenyl isocyanate in dry dichloromethane. This is the chemically matched transformation for the target aryl urea. The listed Boc-protected reactant cannot directly give the product because the Boc tert-butoxycarbonyl group is absent from the product and blocks the required amine nucleophile.

If the free amine is isolated as an HCl or other acid salt, the same isocyanate coupling can be run with 1.1-2.0 equiv of DIPEA or triethylamine in dry dichloromethane. This is also plausible, but base should be avoided unless needed because the neutral free amine should react cleanly without it.

Using the originally proposed Boc-protected reactant directly with 3-chlorophenyl isocyanate is not recommended. The alpha-nitrogen is protected as a Boc carbamate and is not the free amine required for urea formation; this also fails atom conservation because the tert-butyl/Boc atoms have no place in the product.

solvents.name: dichloromethane
solvents.volume: 10 mL per 1.0 mmol of free amino tryptophan N-methylamide

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, charge an oven-dried flask with free amino tryptophan N-methylamide, CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)N, 1.0 equiv. Add dry dichloromethane, 10 mL per 1.0 mmol substrate, to give an approximately 0.1 M solution. Add 3-chlorophenyl isocyanate, O=C=Nc1cccc(Cl)c1, 1.1 equiv, preferably as a solution in a small portion of dichloromethane, and stir at 25 °C for 4 hours. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC for disappearance of the free amine. After completion, quench any residual isocyanate with a small amount of methanol, concentrate, and purify the residue by silica gel chromatography, for example dichloromethane/methanol or ethyl acetate/hexanes with a small amount of amine modifier if needed, to afford CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)Nc1cccc(Cl)c1.
